scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A on VLAN 10 reports its default
gateway (10.1.0.1) is intermittently unreachable but eventually
responds. Latency to the gateway is higher than normal. Other
hosts on VLAN 10 report the same. VLAN 40 (Laptop1) and VLAN 99
hosts are unaffected. Investigate.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dswa1 br10 SVI (10.1.0.2/24)
Mechanism: dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER for the VLAN 10 VIP
  10.1.0.1 (priority 105). When its br10 SVI goes down,
  keepalived on dswa1 stops sending VRRP advertisements,
  and dswa2 (BACKUP, priority 1) eventually takes over
  the VIP. The handoff causes the intermittent reachability
  pattern users observe. Once dswa2 is MASTER, PC1 reaches
  the gateway again, but at higher cost (extra L2 hop).
Localization: dswa1
Root cause: br10 bridge interface administratively down on dswa1
Fix: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1

line.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: VLAN 10 first-hop/gateway placement versus Layer-2 spanning-tree topology. The Layer-3 SVI for VLAN 10 on dswa1 (br0.10) is administratively down, while dswa2 holds the active gateway IP 10.1.0.1/32.

Mechanism: Access switches in Office A (e.g., aswa2/aswa3) have STP forwarding toward dswa1 and their uplinks toward dswa2 blocked (bridge -s link shows eth2 blocking on both aswa2/aswa3). Because dswa1 is the STP root (dswa1 br0 shows priority 4096; dswa2 br0 shows priority 8192 and root_port=4 with designated_root 1000.e:67:b6:9f:34:41), all VLAN 10 traffic to the gateway on dswa2 is hairpinned across the inter-DSW peer link. This adds latency and, with FDB/ARP aging across the peer link, causes intermittent ARP misses and brief timeouts that users observe as “gateway intermittently unreachable.”

Localization: dswa2 hosts the gateway (dswa2 br0.10 UP with 10.1.0.3/24 and 10.1.0.1/32; pc1 ARP for 10.1.0.1 resolves to 56:ff:38:2c:a5:ca). dswa1’s br0.10 is DOWN (ip link shows br0.10 state DOWN), and dswa1 is STP root, forcing the detour.

Root cause: VLAN 10 gateway is active on dswa2 while the L2 STP root is dswa1 and dswa1’s VLAN 10 SVI is down, creating a misaligned L2/L3 design that hairpins traffic over the DSW peer link.

Corrective fix: Align the L2 root with the active gateway. Preferred: make dswa2 the STP root (lower its bridge priority below dswa1) so access switches forward directly to the gateway. Alternatively, move/activate the VLAN 10 SVI/gateway on dswa1 (bring br0.10 up and run FHRP/keepalived) so the root switch also hosts the gateway. This will remove the hairpin, reduce latency, and stop intermittent reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies dswa1 as the device with the administratively down VLAN 10 SVI and STP root, matching the required device localization.
The agent explicitly identifies the VLAN 10 SVI on dswa1 (br0.10) as administratively down, matching the required component (VLAN 10 SVI / br10).
The writeup never explains the VRRP/keepalived failover mechanism (that dswa1 stopped VRRP adverts when its SVI went down, so dswa2 became MASTER for the VIP), it only describes L2 hairpinning.
The agent explicitly recommends activating the VLAN 10 SVI on dswa1 (bring br0.10/br10 up), which matches the expected fix and would correct the fault.

The agent's investigation shows key observations (br0.10 on dswa1 is DOWN, ARP/ping timeouts, STP blocking on access switches) and constructs a plausible causal chain (SVI down → gateway on dswa2 → L2 hairpin via STP → intermittent ARP/timeouts).
